title: The module-level flat cotorsion pair on a small ringed site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. In $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $\mathcal F$ be the tensor-flat sheaves [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and put $\mathcal T=\mathcal F^{\perp_1}$. Here $\operatorname{Ext}^1(U,V)=0$ means that every short exact sequence $0\to V\to E\to U\to0$ splits, and right and left $\perp_1$ denote vanishing against every object of the indicated class.
Then $\mathcal F={}^{\perp_1}\mathcal T$. The pair $(\mathcal F,\mathcal T)$ is hereditary: $\operatorname{Ext}^i(F,T)=0$ for every $i\geq1$, $F\in\mathcal F$, $T\in\mathcal T$, with higher Ext interpreted as Yoneda extensions; in particular $\mathcal F$ is closed under kernels of epimorphisms between its objects and $\mathcal T$ under cokernels of monomorphisms between its objects. Both classes are closed under extensions and retracts, and $\mathcal F$ is closed under small coproducts. There is a set $S\subseteq\mathcal F$ such that $\mathcal T=S^{\perp_1}$. There is a flat generator $G\in\mathcal F$, meaning that every object of $\mathcal A$ is an epimorphic image of a small coproduct of copies of $G$. No points or projective objects of the site are assumed.

source.place: Agent-formulated module-level foundation for proof paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction. WANTED: Rene Recktenwald, Construction of Six Functor Formalisms (2019), Theorem 2.5.35 and Proposition 2.5.20, https://d-nb.info/1211326829/34 (read online, not archived). Flat generators: Stacks Tags 03EV (sites-modules-lemma-j-shriek-flat), 03EW (sites-modules-lemma-module-quotient-flat), and 03DA/03DB. No Stacks tag states the cotorsion-pair theorem.

proof.text: By [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], $\mathcal A$ is Grothendieck and has the generator $G=\bigoplus_U j_{U!}R_U$. Each summand is flat by [lem-pc-sites-modules-j-shriek-flat], and its coproduct is flat by [lem-pc-sites-modules-coproduct-flat]. To check the epimorphic-image meaning of generator required here, [lem-pc-sites-modules-quotient-j-shriek] supplies, for each $M$, an epimorphism $\bigoplus_{(U,s)}j_{U!}R_U\to M$. For each pair $(U,s)$ extend its summand map to $G$ by setting its other components equal to zero. The resulting map $\bigoplus_{(U,s)}G\to M$ is epic because the preceding epimorphism factors through it. Smallness of the site and of every section set makes both index sets small. Consequently every module admits an epimorphism from a flat module, without any assertion that sections of an arbitrary epimorphism are surjective.

source.place: Tags 03DA/03DB, 03EV (lemma-j-shriek-flat), 03EW (lemma-module-quotient-flat); form the sum over all objects.

proof.text: We record the closure calculations needed below. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-quotient-tensor-ses], kernels of epimorphisms between flats are flat. In $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ with $A,C$ flat, that same lemma makes the sequence stay short exact after tensoring with any $N$. For a monomorphism $N\to N^{\prime}$, the diagram of these two tensor sequences has monic left and right vertical maps. Its middle vertical map is monic: locally an element in its kernel maps to zero in $C\otimes N$, so comes from $A\otimes N$, and vanishes by monicity of $A\otimes N\to A\otimes N^{\prime}$ and of $A\otimes N^{\prime}\to B\otimes N^{\prime}$. Thus $B$ is flat; tensor is right exact because it is an additive left adjoint by [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. A retract of a flat module is flat since the tensor map of a monomorphism is then a retract of a monomorphism. Finally filtered colimits of flats are flat: tensor commutes with those colimits by the same tensor-Hom adjunction, and those colimits are exact by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian]. This proves the claims by applying the colimit to the tensor of any short exact sequence. Small coproduct closure was already supplied in Step 1. The zero module is flat since its tensor functor is zero.

source.place: Tags 03EX (lemma-flat-tor-zero), 03EY (lemma-flat-ses), 03EU (lemma-colimits-flat), and 03EP (lemma-tensor-commute-colimits); explicit monomorphism and retract calculations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-small-flat-subsheaf] and fix its infinite bound $\kappa$. Let $S$ contain one representative of each isomorphism class of flat module sheaves of size at most $\kappa$, including zero when it satisfies this bound. These representatives form a set: choose section sets as subsets of a fixed set of cardinal $\kappa$ and encode addition, scalar multiplication and restriction by their graphs. There are only set-many such graphs since the objects, arrows, and ring section sets of the site are sets; the sheaf axiom and flatness just select a subclass of this set. Thus $S\subseteq\mathcal F$. Every nonzero flat quotient encountered below contains a nonzero subobject isomorphic to a member of $S$ and has flat quotient by that subobject.

source.place: Agent set-coding argument; online Recktenwald, Corollary 2.5.33 proof (bounded-subobject part). WANTED: archive this reference.

proof.text: For every flat $F$ construct a continuous filtration $F_0=0\subseteq F_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_\lambda=F$ with flat residual quotients $F/F_\alpha$ and successive factors in $S$ up to isomorphism. At a successor, if $F/F_\alpha\ne0$, choose its nonzero bounded flat subobject $P$ using [lem-coef-small-flat-subsheaf], and take $F_{\alpha+1}$ to be its inverse image in $F$; then $F_{\alpha+1}/F_\alpha=P$ and $F/F_{\alpha+1}=(F/F_\alpha)/P$ are flat. The pullback short exact sequence is the opposite-category form of [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-short-exact-sequence]. At a nonzero limit $\beta$ take the colimit in $\mathcal A$ of the preceding subobjects. Exact filtered colimits from [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] make its map into $F$ monic and identify $F/F_\beta=\varinjlim_{\alpha<\beta}F/F_\alpha$, flat by Step 2. Each nonterminal successor strictly enlarges the subobject, so contributes a section of $F$ not in its predecessor. Distinct successors contribute distinct sections in the disjoint union of the $F(U)$. Therefore the process must stop before the successor cardinal of $|F|$; all the ordinals used are small. For $F=0$ use the length-zero filtration.

source.place: Agent transfinite construction making explicit the filtration used in Recktenwald Lemma 2.5.24/Corollary 2.5.33. WANTED: archive the reference.

proof.text: Let $T\in S^{\perp_1}$ and $0\to T\to E\xrightarrow{p}F\to0$ be an extension, with $F$ flat and filtration as in Step 4. Write $E_\alpha=p^{-1}F_\alpha$; pullback exactness is [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-short-exact-sequence] in the opposite abelian category. We construct compatible sections $s_\alpha:F_\alpha\to E_\alpha$. The initial section is zero. Given $s_\alpha$, put $D=E_{\alpha+1}/s_\alpha(F_\alpha)$. The quotient sequence $0\to T\to D\to F_{\alpha+1}/F_\alpha\to0$ is short exact: $s_\alpha(F_\alpha)$ meets $T$ in zero, and a section whose projection lies in $F_\alpha$ differs, locally, from its $s_\alpha$ image by a unique section of $T$. Since the last object is isomorphic to a member of $S$, the quotient extension splits. Take its retraction onto $T$ and compose with $E_{\alpha+1}\to D$, obtaining $r:E_{\alpha+1}\to T$ with $r|_T=1$ and $rs_\alpha=0$. The inverse of $\ker(r)\xrightarrow{p}F_{\alpha+1}$ gives $s_{\alpha+1}$ extending $s_\alpha$: for a local lift $e$ of $x$, the inverse is $e-i r(e)$, independent of the lift. At a limit, the compatible maps $F_\alpha\to E$ induce a map $F_\beta\to E$ by the colimit universal property; its composite with $p$ is the inclusion, so it is the required section. The pullback filtrations and their short exact sequences persist at limits by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian]. At the last stage this splits $p$. Hence $S^{\perp_1}\subseteq\mathcal F^{\perp_1}$; the reverse inclusion follows from $S\subseteq\mathcal F$. We have proved $\mathcal T=S^{\perp_1}$, including the empty filtration case, by an explicit compatible-splitting induction.

source.place: Agent proof of the transfinite extension-splitting argument underlying Recktenwald Lemma 2.5.24. No unproved compatibility at limits is asserted.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal L={}^{\perp_1}(S^{\perp_1})={}^{\perp_1}\mathcal T$. By the definition of $\mathcal T$, every flat object, including the generator $G$ of Step 1, lies in $\mathcal L$. The hypotheses of [lem-coef-generating-set-cotorsion-smallness] therefore hold: $\mathcal A$ is Grothendieck by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], $S$ is a set, and $G\in\mathcal L$ is a generator in the epimorphic-image sense. Its filtration/retract conclusion says every $L\in\mathcal L$ is a retract of an $(S\cup\{G\})$-filtered object. Such an object is flat by transfinite induction using the zero, extension and filtered-colimit closure of Step 2, since all its successive factors are flat. Retract closure in Step 2 now gives $L$ flat. Together with the opposite inclusion already noted, this proves $\mathcal F={}^{\perp_1}\mathcal T$. No module-specific cotorsion result is being assumed in the generic theorem.

source.place: Agent alternative to Recktenwald Proposition 2.5.20: apply the existing general set-cogenerated approximation/filtration theorem after the explicit set-detection argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cotorsion-orthogonality-calculus] to the abelian category $\mathcal A$: both left and right Ext-one orthogonals are closed under extensions and retracts and contain zero. Since Step 6 identifies $\mathcal F$ with the left orthogonal of $\mathcal T$ and $\mathcal T=\mathcal F^{\perp_1}$ by definition, this supplies the stated extension/retract closure of both classes. The coproduct closure of $\mathcal F$ is Step 1; its kernel closure is Step 2.

source.place: Agent application of splitting-orthogonal closure; source conventions for extensions: Stacks homology.tex, Section 010I.

proof.text: We prove higher Yoneda vanishing by induction on $n\geq1$, simultaneously for every flat $F$ and every $T\in\mathcal T$. For $n=1$ every extension splits by the definition of $\mathcal T$. For $n\geq2$, take an arbitrary representative $\xi:0\to T\to E_{n-1}\to\cdots\to E_0\to F\to0$. Step 1 supplies a flat epimorphism $P\to E_0$; its composite onto $F$ is epic. Hence $K=\ker(P\to F)$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-quotient-tensor-ses], since both $P$ and $F$ are flat. Apply [lem-coef-yoneda-pullback-splice] with $L=\ker(E_0\to F)$. It supplies an $(n-1)$-extension $\eta$ of $K$ by $T$ whose splice with $0\to K\to P\to F\to0$ represents the same Yoneda class as $\xi$. The induction hypothesis applies to flat $K$, so $\eta$ is zero. By [lem-coef-yoneda-zero-splice], its splice is zero as well. Thus the arbitrary class $\xi$ vanishes, completing the induction without projective covers or points.

source.place: Section Tag 06XP and Definition Tag 06XT, applied to the flat-epimorphism induction of the inherited proof step 8; exact-sequence comparison and zero-splice arguments extracted as separate nodes.

proof.text: For completeness, verify the claimed cokernel closure without importing an unstated long exact Yoneda sequence. Suppose $0\to T_0\to T_1\xrightarrow{q}T_2\to0$ is short exact with $T_0,T_1\in\mathcal T$, and consider an extension $0\to T_2\to E\to F\to0$ with $F$ flat. Choose a flat epimorphism $P\to E$ using Step 1. Put $K=\ker(P\to F)$, flat by [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-quotient-tensor-ses], and let $a:K\to T_2$ be the induced map. Pull back $q$ along $a$; by [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-short-exact-sequence] in the opposite category it is an extension of flat $K$ by $T_0$, so splits. It gives a lift $\widetilde a:K\to T_1$. Push out $0\to K\to P\to F\to0$ along $\widetilde a$ using the same cited theorem. Its result $0\to T_1\to E^{\prime}\to F\to0$ splits because $T_1\in\mathcal T$. Its pushout along $q$ is therefore split and is the pushout of the original $K\to P$ sequence along $a$. That latter pushout is $E$: the maps $T_2\to E$ and $P\to E$ agree on $K$, and any agreeing maps out of $T_2,P$ factor uniquely through $E$ since $P\to E$ is epic with kernel $\ker(a:K\to T_2)$; also $K\to T_2$ is epic by pulling back the epic $P\to E$. This checks the universal property directly. Consequently the original extension splits. This holds for every flat $F$, hence $T_2\in\mathcal T$. All pullbacks and quotients here are in the abelian sheaf category; none requires a sectionwise lift of an arbitrary epimorphism. Steps 1-9 give all clauses of the item.
